title: Table and graph of y=x^3+x^2-5x, and the roots of y=0

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2019), parts (a), (b) and (c) only. Official answers and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The printed grid is not reproduced. Parts (d) (tangent gradient, section 18.6) and (e) are omitted; they are not part of this item. Fully manual.

stem:
This question is 0580/43/O/N/19 Question 3 parts (a), (b) and (c) only, taken from the official QP. Parts (d) and (e) of the printed question are not included here.

The table shows some values for \(y=x^3+x^2-5x\).

The \(x\)-values are \(-3\), \(-2\), \(-1.5\), \(-1\), \(0\), \(1\), \(1.5\), \(2\), \(2.5\), \(3\). The given \(y\)-values are: when \(x=-3\), \(y=-3\); when \(x=-2\), \(y=6\); when \(x=-1.5\), \(y=6.4\); when \(x=0\), \(y=0\); when \(x=1.5\), \(y=-1.9\); when \(x=2\), \(y=2\); when \(x=2.5\), \(y=9.4\). The missing values are those for \(x=-1\), \(x=1\) and \(x=3\).

(a) Complete the table.

(b) On a grid, draw the graph of \(y=x^3+x^2-5x\) for \(-3\leqslant x\leqslant 3\).

(c) Use your graph to solve the equation \(x^3+x^2-5x=0\).

steps.name: C
steps.text_tex: (b) Plot the points from the completed table and join them with a smooth cubic curve.
steps.note: MS 3(b): Fully correct curve, 4 marks; B3 FT for 9 or 10 points, B2 FT for 7 or 8 points, B1 FT for 5 or 6 points.

steps.name: R1
steps.note: MS 3(c): –2.9 to –2.7, 0, and 1.7 to 1.9, 2 marks, B1 for 2 correct values.

steps.name: R2
steps.text_tex: The other two solutions, read from the graph, are in the intervals \(-2.9\) to \(-2.7\) and \(1.7\) to \(1.9\).
steps.note: Official acceptable ranges from the MS. The exact roots are not required.
